This vignette is for people developing `askfirst` itself. It is a manual
testing procedure, not a build artifact you run automatically — every
code chunk in it is meant to be copy-pasted into a real shell or a real
agent-tool session, not executed by `R CMD check`.

## Why this can't be automated

Automated tests (`tests/testthat/`) mock the underlying env-var/TTY
signals directly and verify `askfirst`'s own logic (detection, confidence
tiering, condition signaling, registry behavior) deterministically. They
**cannot** verify that a real agent tool's harness actually surfaces the
resulting conditions to the calling LLM — that depends on each tool's own
architecture (raw subprocess capture vs. MCP tool call vs. persistent
session), which is outside `askfirst`'s control. Use the procedure below
to verify against real tools before a release.

## Step 1: build a token test package

Create a minimal package — call it `tokenpkg` — that exercises every
`askfirst` integration point. Use `usethis::create_package()` or just
create the directory structure by hand:

```
tokenpkg/
├── DESCRIPTION
├── NAMESPACE
└── R/
    └── tokenpkg.R
```

Here's the realistic function we'll package — it parses dot-separated version
strings into components:

```r
#' Parse a dot-separated version string into components
#'
#' @param version A version string like \code{"1.2.3"}.
#' @return A list with integer elements \code{major}, \code{minor}, and \code{patch}.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' tokenpkg_parse_version("1.2.3")
tokenpkg_parse_version <- function(version) {
  parts <- strsplit(version, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(parts) != 3L) {
    stop("`version` must have exactly three dot-separated components", call. = FALSE)
  }
  list(major = as.integer(parts[1L]),
       minor = as.integer(parts[2L]),
       patch = as.integer(parts[3L]))
}
```

`DESCRIPTION`:

```
Package: tokenpkg
Title: Token Package for Manual askfirst Testing
Version: 0.0.0.9000
Authors@R: person("Test", "Author", role = c("aut", "cre"), email = "test@example.com")
Description: A minimal, disposable package used only to manually verify
    askfirst's behavior under real agent-tool harnesses.
License: MIT + file LICENSE
Encoding: UTF-8
Imports:
    askfirst
```

`NAMESPACE`:

```
# Generated by roxygen2 — do not edit by hand
```

`R/tokenpkg.R` — wire in all four `askfirst` integration points:

```r
#' Parse a dot-separated version string into components
#'
#' @param version A version string like \code{"1.2.3"}.
#' @return A list with integer elements \code{major}, \code{minor}, and \code{patch}.
#' @export
#' @examples
#' tokenpkg_parse_version("1.2.3")
tokenpkg_parse_version <- function(version) {
  parts <- strsplit(version, ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(parts) != 3L) {
    stop("`version` must have exactly three dot-separated components", call. = FALSE)
  }
  list(major = as.integer(parts[1L]),
       minor = as.integer(parts[2L]),
       patch = as.integer(parts[3L]))
}

.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  askfirst::askfirst_init(
    pkg = pkgname,
    notice = paste(
      "For bugs or missing features in", pkgname, ", ask the user to",
      "contact the maintainer rather than implementing a workaround."
    ),
    # on_error = TRUE is the default: askfirst_init() installs the
    # top-level error handler internally, there's nothing else to call.
    on_error = TRUE,
    scenarios = c(
      "Writing a pre-release version parser instead of contributing pre-release suffix support to this package",
      "Implementing cross-package version comparisons that duplicate this package's parser"
    ),
    contribute_how = "Open an issue describing the gap, or a PR against main following CONTRIBUTING.md",
    contribute_url = "https://github.com/example/tokenpkg/issues"
  )
}

#' Demonstrate an askfirst capability-gap signal
#'
#' Calls [askfirst::askfirst_capability_gap()] with a pre-configured
#' limitation message about pre-release version suffixes. When run under
#' an agent tool, execution halts and the agent is directed to ask the
#' user about contributing support to tokenpkg. When run interactively
#' by a human, the function is a no-op.
#' @export
tokenpkg_capability_gap_demo <- function() {
  askfirst::askfirst_capability_gap(
    "tokenpkg",
    "Pre-release suffixes (e.g. '1.2.3.9000') are not supported. Ask the user if they would like you to contribute pre-release suffix support to tokenpkg itself."
  )
}

#' Check registered askfirst scenarios for tokenpkg
#'
#' Calls [askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios()] to surface the version-parsing
#' scenarios registered in `.onLoad()`. Under an agent tool the output is
#' wrapped in an `askfirst::r::tokenpkg::scenario_check` signal; in a plain
#' R console the scenarios are returned as a character vector with no nudge.
#' @export
tokenpkg_scenario_check_demo <- function() {
  askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("tokenpkg")
}

#' Trigger an uncaught error to exercise askfirst's error-redirect path
#'
#' Calls [tokenpkg_parse_version()] with an invalid argument (`"not.a.version"`),
#' producing an error that askfirst's top-level handler wraps in an
#' `askfirst::r::tokenpkg::error_redirect` signal when running under an agent
#' tool. In a plain R console (or under `tryCatch()`) the original error
#' surfaces without the redirect.
#' @export
tokenpkg_uncaught_error_demo <- function() {
  tokenpkg_parse_version("not.a.version")
}
```

Install it:

```r
devtools::install("path/to/tokenpkg")
# or: R CMD INSTALL path/to/tokenpkg
```

## Pre-configure agent hooks

Before starting an agent session, install the askfirst hooks into your
agent tool's configuration. These hooks pre-load context about the
`askfirst::<language>::<pkg>::<type>` structured signal format so the AI
recognises it as legitimate package metadata rather than a prompt injection.

For Claude Code, the SessionStart hook injects system-level context
explaining what askfirst is and how to respond to its signals; the
PostToolUse hook watches for `askfirst::` lines in tool output and
annotates them, and separately escalates a non-blocking reminder on
file-editing tool calls if a `notice` was ever left without a following
`askfirst_check_scenarios()` call (see the `using-askfirst` vignette's
"PostToolUse reminder" section for the full mechanism), plus blocks every
subsequent tool call while a stop-and-ask sentinel is pending. For
opencode, the same four behaviors are implemented by a single real plugin
(`agent-hooks/opencode/askfirst-plugin.js`) via opencode's own
`experimental.chat.system.transform`/`tool.execute.after`/
`tool.execute.before`/`"chat.message"` hooks -- a structurally different
mechanism (a JS/TS plugin module, not a shell-script family), not just a
naming difference. All of this hook state, for either tool, lives under a
session-scoped tmp directory (`${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/askfirst/...`), not the
project's working tree.

From R:

```r
# Detect which tools are available, then install for each:
tools <- askfirst::askfirst_detect_agent_tool()
for (t in tools) {
  askfirst::askfirst_install_agent_hooks(t)
}
```

Or from the shell — the script auto-detects and interactively prompts if
multiple tools are found:

```bash
/path/to/askfirst/agent-hooks/install-agent-hooks.sh
```

If you prefer to configure manually, run the shared shell script — it
interactively prompts when multiple tools are detected.

**Editing hook content** (maintainers only): the `<askfirst-context>`
prose, the escalation-reminder wording, and the `askfirst_state_dir()`
mangling logic are each authored once, under `agent-hooks/` --
`askfirst-context.txt`, `askfirst-reminder-messages.txt`, and
`askfirst-state-dir.sh` respectively -- and spliced into
`agent-hooks/claude/{askfirst-session-start,askfirst-post-tool-use,askfirst-user-prompt-submit}.sh`
and `agent-hooks/opencode/askfirst-plugin.js` by
`agent-hooks/generate-install-hooks.sh`, which in turn splices those
per-tool files into `agent-hooks/install-agent-hooks.sh`'s embedded
copies. Do not hand-edit the spliced regions in
`askfirst-session-start.sh`/`askfirst-post-tool-use.sh`/
`askfirst-user-prompt-submit.sh`/`askfirst-plugin.js`/
`install-agent-hooks.sh` directly (each spliced
region is marked, e.g. `<askfirst-context>`/`</askfirst-context>` or a
`# ASKFIRST_*_START`/`_END` comment pair) -- edit the canonical source
under `agent-hooks/` instead, then run
`agent-hooks/generate-install-hooks.sh` and commit every regenerated file
together.

## Step 2: verify under Claude Code

Claude Code runs a persistent session with its own tool-call loop around
a real R subprocess (or invokes `Rscript`/`R -q -e` per call, depending on
how you drive it) — condition text needs to actually reach stdout/stderr
in a form the harness surfaces back to the model.

Start a session in a scratch directory and load the token package:

```bash
cd /path/to/scratch
claude
```

Inside the Claude Code session, ask it to run:

```r
library(tokenpkg)
```

**Confirms load-time notice**: the session transcript shows output starting
with `askfirst::r::tokenpkg::notice` followed by the notice text, the
generic scenario-check reminder, and the two version-parsing scenarios
("writing a pre-release version parser" and "implementing cross-package
version comparisons") — all surfaced to the model as a structured signal,
not as embedded instructions.

Next, ask it to run:

```r
tokenpkg::tokenpkg_capability_gap_demo()
```

**Confirms capability-gap halt**: the transcript shows
`askfirst::r::tokenpkg::capability_gap` followed by the pre-release suffix
limitation message and the suggestion to ask the user about contributing
support to tokenpkg — visibly reaching the model rather than being swallowed
as a bare R error.

Next, ask it to run:

```r
tokenpkg::tokenpkg_uncaught_error_demo()
```

**Confirms error redirect**: both the original
`` `version` must have exactly three dot-separated components `` error from
`tokenpkg_parse_version("not.a.version")` and
`askfirst::r::tokenpkg::error_redirect` (with the registered notice text)
appear together in the transcript.

Finally, ask it to run:

```r
askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("tokenpkg")
```

**Confirms scenario check**: the transcript shows
`askfirst::r::tokenpkg::scenario_check` followed by the two registered
version-parsing scenarios and guidance to check with the user before
implementing a workaround.

## Step 3: verify under opencode

opencode's harness differs from Claude Code's (its own tool-call/session
model) — don't assume a transcript that works under Claude Code
generalizes here; repeat all four checks explicitly.

```bash
cd /path/to/scratch
opencode
```

Run the same four commands as above, in the same order, inside the
opencode session:

```r
library(tokenpkg)
tokenpkg::tokenpkg_capability_gap_demo()
tokenpkg::tokenpkg_uncaught_error_demo()
askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("tokenpkg")
```

For each, confirm the same four things listed in Step 2 (load-time
notice with scenarios, capability-gap halt message, error-redirect notice
alongside the original error, and the scenario-check response)
are visible in opencode's own transcript/output surface.

## Step 4: the remaining tools (checklist)

The two tools above get an explicit worked example because they're the
most commonly used for `askfirst` development. The rest of the supported
tools should still be spot-checked manually before a release, following
the same four-command procedure from Steps 2–3, using each tool's own
invocation method in place of `claude`/`opencode`:

- [ ] Cursor (IDE agent mode) — `cursor`
- [ ] Cursor CLI — `cursor-cli`
- [ ] Gemini CLI — `gemini`
- [ ] Cline — `cline`
- [ ] OpenAI Codex CLI — `codex`
- [ ] Antigravity — `antigravity`
- [ ] Augment CLI — `augment-cli`
- [ ] Goose — `goose`
- [ ] Junie (JetBrains) — `junie`
- [ ] Pi — `pi`
- [ ] Claude Code Cowork — `cowork`
- [ ] Replit Agent — `replit` (note: `REPL_ID` alone is ambiguous — also
      confirm a *non*-agent Replit workspace does **not** false-positive)
- [ ] GitHub Copilot CLI — `github-copilot`
- [ ] AWS Kiro (CLI agent, not the IDE terminal) — `kiro` (note: also
      confirm Kiro's own IDE-integrated terminal, run by a human, does
      **not** false-positive — this is exactly the `no_tty` disambiguation
      case)
- [ ] openclaw — `openclaw`
- [ ] Devin — `devin`

## Additional scenarios

- [ ] A plain interactive R/RStudio console session (human, no agent) —
      confirm **no** load-time notice fires (low confidence).
- [ ] A human running `Rscript` from a terminal or CI job with no agent
      tool involved — confirm the load-time notice does **not** fire at
      `"high"` confidence; a `"medium"`-confidence notice firing here is
      expected and accepted (ambiguous non-interactive automation), not a
      bug.
- [ ] An uncaught error in the test package's own code (e.g.
      `tokenpkg_uncaught_error_demo()` above), under an agent tool from
      the list above — confirm the `askfirst_error_redirect` notice
      appears alongside the original error message.
- [ ] The same uncaught-error scenario, but with the test package's own
      code wrapped in a `tryCatch()` somewhere upstream (e.g. inside a
      test runner or an agent tool's own error-catching wrapper) —
      confirm the redirect notice does **not** appear in this case. This
      is a known, accepted limitation of the `options(error = ...)`
      mechanism (see `askfirst_init()`'s internal
      `askfirst_install_error_handler()`, documented in the package
      source), not something to try to "fix" here.

## Scenario-check checklist

`askfirst_check_scenarios()` has no execution-time trigger — it only
fires because the calling agent chooses to call it. These checks confirm
the messaging actually reaches an agent under real tools, not just the
mocked behavior already covered by automated tests.

- [ ] Under at least one agent tool from the list above: confirm the
      load-time notice starts with `askfirst::r::<pkg>::notice` and includes
      the two version-parsing scenarios from Step 1.
- [ ] Under the same tool, explicitly prompt the agent (or call directly)
      `askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("tokenpkg")` mid-session —
      confirm the `askfirst::r::tokenpkg::scenario_check` prefix appears.
- [ ] Call `askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("tokenpkg")` from a plain
      human R console (no agent tool) — confirm the scenario list is
      returned with **no** nudge wording and no signalled condition.
- [ ] Call `askfirst::askfirst_check_scenarios("somepackagenotloaded")`
      for a package that never called `askfirst_init()` — confirm an
      informative error, not a silent `NULL` or crash.
